info.title: Procurement Integrator Sysnet API
info.description:
## Authorization
We use bearer auth throughout the API. Generally, API requests should have the follow header:  
{  
    "content-type": "application/json",  
    "Authorization": "Bearer TOKEN_GOES_HERE"  
}  
Please refer to the Auth section immediately below for details on getting your token.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to group results.
                        The fieldName can be any of the following: purchaseOrderHeaderId, stockId, supplierInventoryCodeId, factorId.
                        The sort could either have - to sort by descending and + to sort by ascending. See groupQuery schema for more info.
                        For grouping using a nested field use <object>.<field> to specify the nested levels eg +Stock.name

parameters.name: groupSummary
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to summarise grouped results by aggregating the groups.
                The fieldName can be any of the following: purchaseOrderDetailId, purchaseOrderHeaderId, stockId, supplierInventoryCodeId, factorId, unitQtyToOrder, qtyToOrder, totalInnersToOrder, costPerOuter, totalCost, qtyInStock, qtyRequired, qtyOnOrder.
                        The type could be count,min,max,sum,avg. See groupSummaryQuery schema for more info.

parameters.name: totalSummary
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to summarise all grouped results by aggregating all the groups sub groups.
                The fieldName can be any of the following: purchaseOrderDetailId, purchaseOrderHeaderId, stockId, supplierInventoryCodeId, factorId, unitQtyToOrder, qtyToOrder, totalInnersToOrder, costPerOuter, totalCost, qtyInStock, qtyRequired, qtyOnOrder.
                        The type could be count,min,max,sum,avg. See groupSummaryQuery schema for more info.

parameters.name: searchDistinct
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to get the distinct values for a field. 
                Only the field specified will be returned in the results. This can be used with filtering functionality, sort and limit. 
                However it cannot be used with group, groupSummary or totalSummary.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to change the sorting of results returned. 
                        The default sort is purchaseOrderDetailId ascending. 
                        Use any fieldNames comma separated in the sort. 
                        Use + for ascending - for descending 
                        eg +updateDateTime.
                        - purchaseOrderDetailId would sort by updateDateTime ascending and then purchaseOrderDetailId descending.
 For sorting using a nested field use <object>.<field> to specify the nested levels eg +Stock.name
                        For sorting using a nested field use <object>.<field> to specify the nested levels eg +Stock.name

post.description:
As a third party system, this API endpoint allows for the creation of invoices in the HAL Sysnet system. It handles validation, processing, and storage of invoice data.

You will need to have the following data accesses assigned to your user to use this route: sc_insert_invoice

dateOrdered.description: Date and time when the order was placed (ISO 8601 format)

purchaseOrderHeaderId.description: Unique ID of the purchase order header

deliveryInstructions.example: Please deliver to loading dock at rear of building

requiredDateTime.description: Date and time when delivery is required (ISO 8601 format)

isCreditClaim.description: Whether the order is a credit claim

companyName.description: Legal name of the company placing the order

purchaseOrderDetailId.description: ID for the specific item in the order

search.name: search
search.description:
This does an advanced search using a url encoded JSON object.

Most fields available in the return object can be searched using this methodology.
Example: search={ "status": "active"} would search the status field for the value: 'active'.

Searching is also possible using nested fields. Use the following syntax: <object>.<field> to specify the nested field.
Example: search={ "Stock.name": "Best Beer" }

There are a couple of extra operators that can be used in the search. These are $or, $and, $not.
Example: search={ "$or": [ { "status": "bad" }, { "status": "worse" } ] }. Searches for the statuses of 'bad' or 'worse'.
The $or, $and and $not operators can be nested.

If the name pair contains a fieldName it is possible for the value to be a sub-object containing any number of operators. The operators depend on the fieldType of the fieldName:

Date time Allowed Operators: $eq, $ne, $is, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $in
Example: search={ "startTime": { "$gt": "2 November 2021" } }

Relative Date time Allowed Operators: $eq, $ne, $is, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $in
Example: search={ "startTime": { "$gt": "2 November 2021" } }
This 'relativeDateTime' field is relative to the timezone a user resides in and is not an absolute point in time

Number Allowed Operators: $eq, $ne, $is, $not, $or, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $between, $notBetween, $in, $notIn
Example: search={ "totalCount": { "$gt": 10 } }

String Allowed Operators: $eq, $ne, $is, $not, $or, $in, $like, $iLike, $notLike, $notILike, $notIn
Example: search={ "failReason": { "$in": ["Out of bounds", "Out of time"] } }

These operators equate to Sequelize operators. See Operators | Sequelize
